title: Recommended centrifuge method for grain size separation in marine sediments
author: Pryor, Tangunan, et al.

steps.title: Pre‑treat lithogenic sediment
steps.instruction: Process the dry <63 µm sieved sediment to remove carbonates, organics, Fe‑Mn coatings and isolate the <2 µm fraction.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 1–2 g of dry sediment that has been sieved to <63 µm.
Remove carbonates (procedure as described in Table 1).
Remove organic matter (procedure as described in Table 1).
Remove any remaining carbonates (procedure as described in Table 1).
Leach Fe‑Mn coatings from the lithogenic fraction (procedure as described in Table 1).
Centrifuge the sample in 50 mL centrifuge tubes to isolate the <2 µm fraction (see Table 1 for detailed centrifugation parameters).
Digest the total dried sample for radiogenic isotope analysis.

steps.title: Pre‑treat biogenic carbonate sediment
steps.instruction: Treat the dry <63 µm sieved sediment with ammonia and centrifuge to isolate the <2 µm biogenic carbonate fraction.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 1–2 g of dry sediment that has been sieved to <63 µm.
Add 40 mL of 0.5 % (v/v) ammonia solution to the sediment.
Centrifuge the mixture in 50 mL centrifuge tubes to isolate the <2 µm fraction (see Table 1 for detailed centrifugation parameters).

steps.title: Measure grain size distribution
steps.instruction: Determine the size distribution of each isolated fraction to verify successful separation.

substeps.instruction: Analyze the 2–10 µm and 10–63 µm size fractions using a Beckman Multisizer IV Coulter Counter; record single‑grain data for the 10 µm range.
Analyze the <2 µm fraction with a HELOS laser particle analyser; confirm that >90 % of the isolated material is clay (<2 µm).
Plot grain‑size distributions on a logarithmic scale.

description: We measured the grain size distribution of the lithogenic sediment to confirm the size isolation was successful. For the 2–10 µm and 10–63 µm size fractions, we use Beckman Multisizer IV Coulter Counter and for the 10 µm, these are single grains based on the data output (see data availability).
